value.zh: 及淮南王允敗，秀因稱石崇、潘岳、歐陽建奉允為亂，收之。
value.en: When Yun fell, Xiu accused Chong, Yue, and Jian of supporting his rebellion and arrested them.
value.literal: When the Prince of Huainan Yun was defeated, Xiu thereupon claimed that Shi Chong, Pan Yue, and Ouyang Jian supported Yun in rebellion and arrested them.

value.en: Chong sighed: "These slaves want my wealth!"
value.literal: Chong sighed: "These slaves covet my wealth!"

value.zh: 收者曰：「知財為禍，何不早散之？」
value.en: The arresters said: "If wealth brings disaster, why not have given it away?"
value.literal: The arresters said: "Knowing wealth brings disaster, why not have dispersed it early?"

value.en: Chong had no answer.
value.literal: Chong could not answer.

value.zh: 初，潘岳母常誚責岳曰：「汝當知足，而乾沒不已乎！」
value.en: Earlier Yue's mother had often scolded him: "Know when you have enough—why keep grasping for more?"
value.literal: Earlier Pan Yue's mother often reproached Yue, saying: "You ought to know sufficiency—why seize and scrape without end!"

value.en: When ruin came Yue told his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."
value.literal: When disaster came Yue apologized to his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."

value.zh: 遂與崇，建皆族誅，籍沒崇家。
value.en: Yue, Chong, and Jian were executed to the clan, and Chong's estate was confiscated.
value.literal: Thereupon Yue, Chong, and Jian were all executed to the clan, and Chong's property was confiscated.

value.zh: 相國倫收淮南王母弟吳王晏，欲殺之。
value.en: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, younger brother of Yun's mother, intending to kill him.
value.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, younger brother of the Prince of Huainan's mother, intending to kill him.

value.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗爭之於朝堂，眾皆諫止倫，倫乃貶晏為賓徒縣王。
value.en: Household Grandee Fu Zhi argued for him in court; all remonstrated, and Lun degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu.
value.literal: The Household Grandee Fu Zhi contended for him in the court hall; all remonstrated and stopped Lun, and Lun thereupon degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu county.

value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.
value.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.

value.en: In summer, in the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell gravely ill;
value.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell ill;

value.en: and in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his condition turned critical.
value.literal: in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his illness became critical.

value.zh: 或詐為尚書符，敕宮門無得內宰相；
value.en: Someone forged a Secretariat order barring chief ministers from entering the palace gates;
value.literal: Someone forged an order in the name of the Secretariat forbidding the palace gates to admit the chief ministers;

value.en: and everyone turned pale with alarm.
value.literal: all turned pale.

value.en: Yu Bing said, "This must be a forgery."
value.literal: Yu Bing said, "This must be a fraud."

value.en: Investigation proved that it was.
value.literal: On investigation, it proved so.

value.en: The emperor's two sons, Pi and Yi, were both still infants.
value.literal: The emperor's two sons Pi and Yi were both still in swaddling clothes.

value.zh: 庾冰自以兄弟秉權日久，恐易世之後，親屬愈疏，為它人所間，每說帝以國有強敵，宜立長君；
value.en: Yu Bing, knowing that he and his brothers had held power for years, feared that after a change of reign their kin would be pushed aside and others would come between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful foes abroad the throne should pass to a mature heir.
value.literal: Yu Bing, considering that he and his brothers had held power long, feared that after a change of reign kinsmen would grow more distant and others would drive wedges between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful enemies abroad the state should install an elder sovereign;

value.zh: 請以母親弟琅邪王岳為嗣，帝許之。
value.en: He proposed the emperor's younger uterine half-brother, Prince Yue of Langye, as successor, and the emperor agreed.
value.literal: he asked that the emperor's younger maternal half-brother, Prince of Langye Yue, be made heir, and the emperor assented.

value.zh: 中書令何充曰：「父子相傳，先王舊典，易之者鮮不致亂。
value.en: He Chong, Director of the Secretariat, said, "Passing the throne from father to son is the ancient royal norm; those who alter it seldom avoid turmoil.
value.literal: Zhongshu Ling He Chong said, "Father-to-son succession is the ancient royal norm; those who change it rarely escape disorder.

value.zh: 故武王不授聖弟，非不愛也。
value.en: King Wu did not enthrone his gifted younger brother—not because he loved him less.
value.literal: Therefore King Wu did not give the throne to his sage younger brother—not from lack of love.

value.zh: 今琅邪踐阼，將如孺子何！」
value.en: If Prince Langye takes the throne, what will become of these infant princes!"
value.literal: If Langye now ascends the throne, what is to become of the infant sons!"

value.en: Bing would not heed him.
value.literal: Bing would not listen.

value.zh: 下詔，以岳為嗣，並以弈繼琅邪哀王。
value.en: An edict named Yue as heir and assigned Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.
value.literal: An edict was issued making Yue the heir and also assigning Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.

value.zh: 壬辰，冰、充及武陵王晞、會稽王昱、尚書令諸葛恢並受顧命。
value.en: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Zhuge Hui, Director of the Secretariat, all received the emperor's deathbed commission.
value.literal: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Shangshu Ling Zhuge Hui all received the dying emperor's charge.

value.en: On guǐsì the emperor died.
value.literal: On guǐsì, the emperor died.

value.en: He had come to the throne as a child and had not personally directed routine affairs;
value.literal: The emperor had succeeded young and did not personally handle routine government;

value.en: but as he matured he showed real virtue in diligence and frugality.
value.literal: when he grew up he showed considerable virtue in diligence and frugality.

value.zh: 帝疾篤，庾冰、庾翼欲立會稽王昱為嗣；
value.en: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;
value.literal: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;

value.zh: 中書監何充建議立皇子聃，帝從之。
value.en: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.
value.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.

value.zh: 九月，丙申，立聃為皇太子。
value.en: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.
value.literal: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.

value.en: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.
value.literal: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.

value.zh: 己亥，何充以遺旨奉太子即位，大赦。
value.en: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.
value.literal: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.

value.en: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.
value.literal: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.

value.en: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.
value.literal: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.

value.zh: 時穆帝方二歲，太后臨朝稱制。
value.en: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.
value.literal: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.

value.zh: 何充加中書監，錄尚書事。
value.en: He Chong was additionally made director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.
value.literal: He Chong was additionally made Director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.

value.zh: 充自陳既錄尚書，不宜復監中書；
value.en: Chong himself stated that having authority to record Masters of Writing affairs, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;
value.literal: Chong himself stated that having authority to record the Masters of Writing, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;

value.en: this was granted, and he was additionally made palace attendant.
value.literal: this was granted, and he was additionally made Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 詔征衛將軍褚裒，欲以為揚州刺史、錄尚書事。
value.en: An edict summoned Defender-General Chu Pou, intending to appoint him Governor of Yangzhou and Recorder of the Secretariat.
value.literal: An edict summoned Defender-General Chu Pou, intending to make him Governor of Yangzhou and Recorder of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 吏部尚書劉遐、長史王胡之說裒曰：「會稽王令德雅望，國之周公也，足下宜以大政授之。」
value.en: Minister of the Civil Service Liu Xia and chief clerk Wang Huzhi urged Pou: "The Prince of Kuaiji's virtue and reputation make him the state's Duke of Zhou; you ought to entrust supreme authority to him."
value.literal: Minister of the Civil Service Liu Xia and Chief Clerk Wang Huzhi urged Pou, saying: "The Prince of Kuaiji's virtue and elegant reputation make him the Duke of Zhou of the state; you ought to entrust great affairs to him."

value.en: Pou then firmly declined and returned to his fief.
value.literal: Pou then firmly declined and returned to his fief.

value.zh: 壬戌，以會稽王昱為撫軍大將軍，錄尚書六條事。
value.en: On renxu the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, was made General of Agitating the Army and Recorder of the Six Secretariat Articles.
value.literal: On renxu, the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, was made General of Agitating the Army and Recorder of Six Articles of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 昱清虛寡慾，尤善玄言，常以劉惔、王濛及穎川韓伯為談客，又辟郗超為撫軍掾，謝萬為從事中郎。
value.en: Yu was pure and sparing of desire, especially skilled in Dark Learning; he often took Liu Tan, Wang Meng, and Han Bo of Yingchuan as conversationalists, and also appointed Xi Chao as staff officer of the Agitating Army and Xie Wan as Secretariat Attendant.
value.literal: Yu was pure and sparing of desires, especially skilled in Dark Learning; he often took Liu Tan, Wang Meng, and Yingchuan's Han Bo as conversation guests; he also appointed Xi Chao as staff officer of the Agitating Army and Xie Wan as Secretariat Attendant.

value.zh: 超，鑒之孫也，少卓犖不羈。
value.en: Chao was Xi Jian's grandson; in youth he was outstanding and unrestrained.
value.literal: Chao was the grandson of Xi Jian; in youth he was outstanding and unrestrained.

value.zh: 父愔，簡默沖退而嗇於財，積錢至數千萬，嘗開庫任超所取；
value.en: His father Xi Yin was plain, silent, retiring, and miserly, amassing cash to tens of millions; he once opened the treasury and let Chao take as he wished;
value.literal: His father Xi Yin was plain, silent, retiring, and stingy with wealth, amassing cash to tens of millions; he once opened the treasury and let Chao take as he wished;

value.en: Chao distributed it to kin and friends and in a single day spent it all.
value.literal: Chao distributed it to kin and friends and in one day spent it all.

value.zh: 萬，安之弟也，清曠秀邁，亦有時名。
value.en: Wan was Xie An's younger brother—pure, open, and elegantly lofty—and he too enjoyed a reputation of the day.
value.literal: Wan was the younger brother of Xie An; pure, open, and elegantly lofty, he too had a name of the age.

value.zh: 丹楊尹劉惔每奇溫才，然知其有不臣之志，謂會稽王昱曰：「溫不可使居形勝之地，其位號常宜抑之。」
value.en: Governor of Danyang Liu Tan often marveled at Wen's talent, yet knew he harbored disloyal ambitions; he told the Prince of Kuaiji: "Wen must not be placed in a strategically decisive post; his rank and title should constantly be held down."
value.literal: Governor of Danyang Liu Tan often marveled at Wen's talent, yet knew he harbored unruly ambitions; he told the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu: "Wen must not be placed in a strategically decisive region; his rank and title should constantly be kept down."

value.zh: 勸昱自鎮上流，以己為軍司，昱不聽；
value.en: He urged Yu personally to guard the upper reaches, with Tan himself as army marshal; Yu would not listen;
value.literal: He urged Yu personally to guard the upper reaches, with Tan himself as army marshal; Yu would not listen;

value.en: He asked again to go himself—again Yu would not listen.
value.literal: he asked again to go himself—again Yu would not listen.

value.zh: 二月，癸丑，以左光祿大夫蔡謨領司徒，與會稽王昱同輔政。
value.en: In the second month, on guichou, Left Household Grandee Cai Mo was made acting Minister of Education, to assist government jointly with the Prince of Kuaiji.
value.literal: Second month, on guichou, Left Household Grandee Cai Mo was made acting Minister of Education, jointly assisting government with the Prince of Kuaiji.

value.zh: 褚裒薦前光祿大夫顧和、前司徒左長史殷浩；
value.en: Chu Pou recommended former Household Grandee Gu He and former left chief clerk of the Minister of Education Yin Hao;
value.literal: Chu Pou recommended former Household Grandee Gu He and former Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Yin Hao;

value.zh: 三月，丙子，以和為尚書令，浩為建武將軍、揚州刺史。
value.en: In the third month, on bingzi, He was made Director of the Secretariat and Hao General of Establishing Martial Prowess and Governor of Yangzhou.
value.literal: Third month, on bingzi, He was made Director of the Secretariat and Hao made General of Establishing Martial Prowess and Governor of Yangzhou.

value.zh: 和有母喪，固辭不起，謂所親曰：「古人有釋衰絰從王者，以其才足干時故也。
value.en: He was in mourning for his mother and firmly declined office; he told those close to him: "In antiquity some cast off mourning bands to follow kings because their talent sufficed to sustain the age.
value.literal: He was in mourning for his mother and firmly declined to take office; he told those close to him: "In antiquity some cast off mourning bands to follow kings because their talent sufficed to sustain the age.

value.zh: 如和者，正足以虧孝道、傷風俗耳。」
value.en: One like me would only impair filial duty and harm custom."
value.literal: One like He would only enough to impair filial duty and harm custom."

value.en: Those of insight praised him.
value.literal: Those of insight praised him.

value.en: Hao also firmly declined.
value.literal: Hao also firmly declined.

value.zh: 會稽王昱與浩書曰：「屬當厄運，危弊理極，足下沈識淹長，足以經濟。
value.en: The Prince of Kuaiji wrote to Hao: "We face ill fortune; peril and decay have reached their limit. Your profound knowledge and long experience are enough to sustain the state.
value.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, wrote to Hao: "We face ill fortune; peril and decay have reached their limit. You have profound knowledge and long experience, enough to sustain the state.

value.zh: 若復深存挹退，苟遂本懷，吾恐天下之事於此去矣。
value.en: If you again deeply preserve modest withdrawal and simply follow your original wish, I fear the realm's affairs will slip away at this very moment.
value.literal: If you again deeply preserve modest withdrawal and simply follow your original wish, I fear the affairs of the realm at this point will pass away.

value.zh: 足下去就，即時之廢興，則家國不異，足下宜深思之。」
value.en: Your going or staying at this moment is the rise or fall of the age; family and state are one—you should ponder this deeply."
value.literal: Your going or staying at this moment is the rise or fall of the age; then family and state are not different—you should ponder this deeply."

value.en: Hao then took office.
value.literal: Hao then took office.
